notes: d9mt is D3D9 straight onto Metal: it replaces DXVK and the Vulkan driver
under it, not just one of them. See docs/d9mt.md.
Upstream declares no license. Its driver/ is extracted DXVK 3.0 (zlib)
and its bridge/ is vendored winemetal from DXMT, but the tree itself says
nothing, so nothing from it may be redistributed in a release until it does.

why: d9mt v1, which the v2 scripts resolve as $ROOT — v2 was extracted out
of it and kept the references. They read tools/make-builtin.py, which
marks the PE dlls as Wine builtins (behind an `if [ -f ]`, so a v2
checkout outside it silently skips the marking and the builtins then
do not load), and vendor/spirv-cross, which the AIR compiler includes.
So the v2 checkout goes inside it — but beside v1's own tracked v2/, which is an older in-repo version, not at it.
The extraction source, cloned to v2/DXVK-3.0-uptsream. Two jobs:
build-driver.sh links against its src/d3d9/d3d9.def for the exports,
and fetch-deps.sh vendors its d3d9 frontend, util/spirv/wsi and the
fetch-deps.sh would clone whatever main is that day, which left two
stagings of the same d9mt commit different drivers; tools/d9mt/build.sh
clones this commit first and hands fetch-deps.sh the result, so the
clone is pinned. v3.0.2 is the nominal base, but upstream vendors from
main, so main's commit is what is pinned here.
Built as x86_64 static libs by build-llvm-unixside.sh, for the AIR
emitter on Wine's unix side. Pinned by the upstream script, not here.
Separate from Homebrew's llvm@15, which build-air-compiler.sh needs
for its host-side llvm-config — both are required.

crossOver: the unix side against that tree's ntdll.so. The link is -undefined
dynamic_lookup, so nothing binds to those files — but the Wine unixlib
ABI the bridge was compiled for is CrossOver's, and the runtime here is
Wine 11.18. Nothing checks that the two agree.
